A1.justification: Both 19-page PDFs contain the same EfficientNav study, including references and Appendices A–H. Complete text and rendered-page comparisons establish that only the first-page arXiv version/date stamp and its associated version link differ.

before.justification: v2.pdf reports original HM3D/Habitat navigation accuracy and latency experiments in Section 4, including component and memory-budget ablations. Appendix E reports an additional retrieval-model comparison.

after.justification: v3.pdf retains the same original navigation experiments and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendix E.

M1.justification: Sections 3.2–3.4 retain identical discrete memory caching, attention-based clustering and semantics-aware retrieval procedures. The model architectures and planning examples in the appendices also match.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same zero-shot object-goal navigation task on HM3D using Habitat and RGB-D observations. No dataset, domain or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is identical in Tables 2, 3 and 6, including LFG, GPT-4 Planner, vLLM, Minference and FlexPrefill. Appendix E retains the same MPNet, MiniLM and LLM retrieval alternatives.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same SR, SPL, real-time latency and end-to-end latency metrics, model configurations and hardware settings. The memory-budget experiments and other testing procedures are unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablation in Table 4, memory-budget sensitivity in Table 5, cache analysis in Figure 10 and retrieval-model ablation in Appendix E are identical. No supplementary analysis or case study changes.

E5.justification: Repeated-trial and uncertainty reporting are unchanged, including Figure 6's 15 navigation trials per final goal with different starting points. No seed information, confidence intervals or significance reporting is added or revised.

E6.justification: All numerical results and plotted findings match, including Appendix E. For example, EfficientNav-34b retains SR 80.0, SPL 41.5, real-time latency 0.87 seconds and end-to-end latency 12.51 seconds in Tables 2–3.

T1.justification: The group-selection objective and memory constraint in Equations 1–2, the cache-hit-rate definition and Appendix A's attention and KV-cache mathematics are identical. No assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain identical contributions and claims about efficient on-device zero-shot navigation, the three proposed components and their reported accuracy and latency advantages.

C2.justification: Explanations of retrieval, clustering and cache reuse are unchanged. Section 5 and Appendices G–H retain the same limitations concerning latency, cloud communication and privacy, and specialized knowledge.

D1.justification: The architecture details, GPU assignments, Jetson deployment and detection model in Appendices D and F match. Planning examples and the code-access URL and link target are also unchanged.

R1.justification: Section 2, the cited works and the complete reference list are identical. Positioning relative to prior navigation systems and efficient-LLM techniques is unchanged.

P1.justification: The first-page arXiv stamp changes from v2 dated 27 November 2025 to v3 dated 17 March 2026, with its version link updated accordingly. All manuscript prose, headings and document structure remain identical.

P2.justification: Figures 1–11 and Tables 1–8 retain identical content, captions, formatting and placement. Rendered pages 2–19 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in the stamp text, with no layout revision.

improvement.justification: The scientific content, experimental evidence, reproducibility information and presentation are unchanged throughout the main text and appendices. Updating the arXiv version/date stamp and its link produces no meaningful difference in overall paper quality.
